# The core parameter ontology

Common operating-condition parameters for mobile, manipulation and marine robots.

31 parameters (leaves) in 18 groups. Roots are the ODD categories; a parameter's category is its root.

## Naming conventions

- Ids are snake_case and name the measured quantity, not the situation: `turbidity`, not `murky_water`; `current_speed`, not `strong_current`.
- Reuse an existing leaf whenever it measures the same quantity, even if the wording or unit differs. Its aliases list the wordings already seen.
- Don't create near-duplicates (`water_clarity` next to `turbidity`). If a quantity is new, say which group it belongs under.
- Booleans are named for the condition that is true (`comms_loss`, `glare`).
- Units go in `unit`, never in the id.

## Units

- Use SI or the unit the ontology already uses for that quantity. Units in this ontology: `1/m^2`, `NTU`, `deg`, `degC`, `kg`, `lux`, `m`, `m/s`, `m^2`, `mm`, `mm/h`, `ms`.
- A leaf's range is its physical bounds, in its unit. An ODD narrows the range to the conditions it covers; convert units before narrowing (knots to m/s, F to degC).
- Fractions and probabilities are unitless in [0, 1].

## Distributions

The nominal frequency of each value in deployment:

- Numeric: `uniform`, `normal(mu, sigma)`, `loguniform` (min > 0; for quantities spanning orders of magnitude), `triangular(mode)`, `beta(a, b)` (on the range).
- Categorical: `uniform`, or `weights` aligned with `values`.
- Boolean: `bernoulli(p)`, p = probability of true.
- Omit the distribution when the description gives no basis; uniform is assumed.

## Grounding

- `sim`: the simulator parameter the value sets.
- `runtime`: the on-robot signal that measures it (a topic or path), used by runtime monitors to check the robot stays inside the ODD.

## Branches

| Branch | Covers | Groups | Parameters | Reference |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `environment` | The world around the robot. | `light`, `weather`, `water`, `water_optical`, `water_motion`, `water_site`, `terrain`, `space`, `people` | 20 | [references/environment.md](references/environment.md) |
| `platform` | The robot itself: speed limits, payload, power. | - | 3 | [references/platform.md](references/platform.md) |
| `task` | What the robot is asked to do. | - | 2 | [references/task.md](references/task.md) |
| `sensors` | Perception and localization capabilities. | `perception`, `localization` | 3 | [references/sensors.md](references/sensors.md) |
| `faults` | Degradations and failures. | `sensor_faults`, `comms_faults` | 3 | [references/faults.md](references/faults.md) |

Load a branch's reference file before drafting a parameter in it.

## Worked examples

1. "illumination" is `lighting` (environment → light → lighting):

   ```yaml
   - name: lighting
     category: environment
     type: continuous
     unit: lux
     range: [0.1, 100000]   # narrow to what the description says
     distribution: loguniform
     grounding: {sim: lighting_lux}
   ```

2. "speed limit" is `max_speed` (platform → max_speed):

   ```yaml
   - name: max_speed
     category: platform
     type: continuous
     unit: m/s
     range: [0, 5]   # narrow to what the description says
   ```

3. "route length" is `goal_distance` (task → goal_distance):

   ```yaml
   - name: goal_distance
     category: task
     type: continuous
     unit: m
     range: [0, 1000]   # narrow to what the description says
   ```

4. A quantity with no leaf ("gap between jacket legs"): don't force it onto the nearest leaf. Pick the group it belongs under (here `task`), and draft a new parameter with a snake_case id, a one-line definition, unit, physical bounds and aliases. It is proposed as a new ontology entry for a human to approve.
